title: Ask for the size first
description:
Write a function that follows the Win32 "call twice" buffer convention, and a caller that uses it correctly.

```
first call with no buffer: needs 14 characters (13 and the terminator)
second call with 14: copied "Hello, Xenon!", returned 13
call with 5: nothing copied, returned 14 (too small)
```
hints: Win32 pages say whether sizes count characters or bytes, and whether they include the terminator; decide yours and write it down (lesson 3.02).
In the caller, the text could change between the two calls, so loop until the second call succeeds.
requirements: `unsigned getGreeting(char* buffer, unsigned size)`: with too small a buffer (or `nullptr`) it writes nothing and returns the size needed; otherwise it copies and returns the length without the terminator.
The caller asks once for the size, makes a `std::vector<char>` and asks again.
Write the documentation comment in the style of a Win32 page, including the return value cases.
stretch: Make a `std::string getGreetingString()` wrapper that hides the two calls.
